results.title: HL7 vs DICOM: Decoding the Backbone of Healthcare IT
results.content: Here come two essential heroes: **HL7 (Health Level Seven)** and **DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine)**, the standards that streamline workflows. HL7 and DICOM serve different purposes in healthcare IT. **HL7 facilitates the exchange of clinical and administrative data, such as patient records and lab results, whereas DICOM focuses on managing diagnostic imaging, including storing and sharing X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans. They bridge the clinical and imaging workflows, ensuring seamless access and data sharing.**. HL7 and DICOM are crucial for healthcare IT but focus on different aspects of healthcare data and workflows. While HL7 manages clinical and administrative data, DICOM specializes in medical imaging. HL7 in healthcare is the standard for exchanging clinical and administrative data. DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine): DICOM is the global standard for handling medical imaging data. On the other hand, DICOM specializes in managing medical imaging data. It ensures that all clinical data, such as patient admission, lab order management, scheduling, and billing, is updated and accessible across departments. DICOM relies on binary data formats to manage large imaging files. A DICOM file includes the image itself and metadata, ensuring the preservation of visual data and its context during transmission. HL7’s workflows involve clinical data. DICOM manages binary image data. DICOM and HL7 serve distinct purposes; however, proper integration is crucial for efficient and unified workflow. Integrating HL7 and DICOM ensures that healthcare providers have a holistic view of the patient’s condition, improving the accuracy and efficiency of diagnoses. DICOM manages the imaging process once the HL7 message reaches the radiology system. DICOM acquires, stores, and transmits the resulting images, ensuring they are compatible with **PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication Systems)** and other viewing systems. Integrating HL7 and DICOM helps healthcare providers deliver seamless, patient-centered care. HL7 uses text-based messages to encode patient and clinical data, while DICOM uses binary formats to manage imaging files. Integrating clinical and imaging data requires strong security measures to protect sensitive patient information. Healthcare IT systems require regular updates to stay compatible with evolving HL7 and DICOM standards. Our cloud-based platform bridges the gap between clinical and imaging data, ensuring real-time access, enhanced collaboration, and secure interoperability.

results.title: The True Value of Seamless HL7 and DICOM Integration - Emergent Connect
results.content: # The True Value of Seamless HL7 and DICOM Integration. Seamless HL7 and DICOM integration transforms imaging workflows by reducing errors, accelerating turnaround times, and improving data consistency. For radiology groups, imaging centers, and enterprise health systems, **seamless HL7 and DICOM integration** is not just a technical convenience—it’s a clinical imperative. From faster study routing to improved diagnostic accuracy, the impact of interoperability between your imaging systems and your EMR or RIS cannot be overstated. ## Understanding HL7 and DICOM: The Backbone of Imaging Interoperability. Together, HL7 and DICOM form the foundation of modern imaging workflows. When imaging systems are not tightly integrated with hospital or clinic systems:. According to the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC), inefficient interoperability results in increased medical errors and unnecessary imaging repeat rates—directly affecting patient safety and revenue integrity. ## The Benefits of Seamless HL7 and DICOM Integration. With bi-directional HL7 integration, orders and results flow automatically between your RIS, PACS, and EMR. When paired with DICOM integration, studies are immediately available for review—eliminating bottlenecks caused by manual uploads or disconnected systems. Seamless integration ensures patient demographics and order details are consistent across platforms, reducing duplication errors and minimizing the need for manual data reconciliation. Radiologists no longer need to toggle between systems or verify patient data across platforms. A tightly integrated workflow enables faster reads and better use of worklists, particularly when supported by intelligent features like Emergent Connect’s PriorityWorklist. Results can be routed instantly to EHRs via HL7, ensuring that primary care physicians, specialists, and clinical teams get imaging insights when and where they need them—supporting faster decision-making and improving patient outcomes. As your imaging operation scales, seamless integration means new facilities or modalities can be onboarded without extensive reconfiguration or vendor-specific limitations. ## Emergent Connect’s Approach to HL7 and DICOM Integration. Our platform supports robust HL7 and DICOM integration designed to streamline clinical workflows while ensuring compliance, scalability, and security. By removing integration barriers, we help radiology groups and imaging centers reduce turnaround times, lower costs, and improve the quality of care. Investing in seamless HL7 and DICOM integration isn’t just a tech decision—it’s a strategic advantage.

results.title: On-Prem vs. Cloud SAST: What Security Leaders Need to Know Before They Migrate
results.content: Cloud SAST: What Security Leaders Need to Know Before They Migrate. The debate over on prem vs cloud security solutions is no longer just theoretical. As cloud-native development becomes the default, the traditional strengths of on prem security are being re-evaluated against newer demands. Whether you’re actively planning a migration or defending your current setup, it’s essential to understand the real tradeoffs in cloud vs on prem SAST models, including how each impacts long-term agility, control, and integration across performance, compliance, scalability, and control. Let’s break down what matters most when comparing on prem vs cloud SAST environments. ## **Why AppSec Teams Can’t Afford to Ignore the On Prem vs Cloud Question**. As the balance between cloud security vs on prem security shifts, teams must consider which model better supports their velocity, compliance posture, and developer experience.. ## **Core Considerations in the On Prem vs Cloud SAST Debate**. Checkmarx, for example, supports both fast and in-depth scanning modes in its cloud-based platform, helping teams cover every application with minimal overhead and faster feedback loops. * **Cloud**: Integrates more seamlessly into modern CI/CD pipelines and cloud-native development workflows. That’s why many teams are modernizing their AppSec by shifting from on prem SAST to cloud-native platforms. Integrating cloud-based SAST with existing CI/CD tools, enforcing granular policies, and aligning scans with unique workflows may still require upfront configuration and continuous tuning. Teams should assess how easily a given cloud solution allows policy management, role-based access control, and environment-specific configurations to match their operational model. Cloud-based SAST provides greater flexibility that supports more accurate results and a closer alignment between AppSec policies and developer workflows. Many security leaders find themselves supporting both on prem and cloud SAST tools during a transition period. Comparing cloud vs on prem tradeoffs across these dimensions helps clarify which model best supports your organization’s growth and risk posture. That’s why more AppSec leaders are reassessing their approach to on prem vs cloud security solutions as part of broader digital transformation strategies. ## Curious About the Shift from On-Prem to Cloud-Native SAST?
